header:
Date: 2026-02-11
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Patel, Diego Ramos (Redwood); Maya Reyes, Ethan Lowe, Sofia Martinez, Liam O'Connor (CloudMart)
Recording: yes
Notes: partner integration sync focused on marketplace listing process, reference architecture, and joint technical validation
summary: Redwood and CloudMart reviewed the marketplace listing requirements and the proposed reference architecture for CloudMart's managed marketplace. Key topics: deployment options (hosted vs private), network topology for VPC/on-prem connectors, KMS and audit logging expectations, packaging for CloudMart marketplace, and an initial validation plan. Agreed next steps include sharing RA docs, running a staging perf validation, and security Q&A follow-up.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Wednesday afternoon, I think we all got the calendar invite, quick roll call?
[00:10] Maya (CloudMart): Hi Maya here from CloudMart partnerships.
[00:12] Ethan (CloudMart): Ethan on SE side.
[00:15] Sofia (CloudMart): Sofia, security.
[00:18] Alex: Great, Alex Chen from Redwood, Priya Patel our SE is here and Diego on integrations.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood): hi all, today we want to run through the reference architecture and the steps for getting Redwood listed in CloudMart marketplace — packaging, manifest, entitlements, and a short plan for a validation run.
[00:40] Maya: sounds good, main thing from partners side is we need the RA doc and we need to know if you require any special networking like private connectors or if hosted listing is enough.
[00:52] Diego (Redwood): quick note, there are two common patterns: hosted API listing where customers call Redwood's hosted runtime via API keys provided by marketplace, and a private listing where Redwood runs inside customer VPC via our private deployment connector — that latter requires explicit VPC peering or a connector agent.
[01:10] Ethan: ok, for CloudMart marketplace we prefer marketplace-hosed integrations but we also support private marketplace listings where vendor provides an AMI/container. Need to check the ops constraints.
[01:22] Priya: right, operationally if you go hosted we have a simple auth flow: marketplace issues token, we map to account, entitlements control quotas; if private, you get more control but require a few network steps and KMS integration for key management.
[01:38] Sofia: on the security side, can you summarize SOC2 posture and key rotation? Also curious about audit logs and whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:48] Alex: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, we support forwarding audit logs via syslog/CloudWatch and we integrate with customer KMS for encryption of customer keys on Private. We should share our security pack after this.
[02:05] Maya: yes pls share, and a checklist for the marketplace listing — the product team wants to know the metadata fields we need.
[02:12] Alex: we'll attach the marketplace checklist (manifest fields, icons, screenshots, billing taxonomy). Diego will walk through the RA diagram now.
[02:22] Diego: ok pulling up the RA diagram, note the three layers: control plane (Redwood management), hosting (Redwood runtime or customer-hosted), and network boundary — for private we recommend a NAT + connector pattern so no inbound from public internet.
[02:40] Ethan: that NAT pattern is good, but for customers that require air-gapped we need an on-prem bundle. Do you provide an OVA/container for that?
[02:50] Priya: we do — we have an on-prem package; full air-gap requires a longer engagement for licensing and support. For marketplace listing we can document both options.
[03:04] Sofia: curious about KMS — does Redwood bring keys into your control plane? We need customer-managed keys ideally.
[03:12] Alex: customer-managed KMS is supported on private; on hosted we store encrypted keys and we can support a customer KMS via our HSM integration for enterprise accounts. We'll include that detail in the security doc.
[03:26] Maya: perfect. On billing, the marketplace needs metering endpoints or an invoice file. How do you expose usage?
[03:33] Priya: we have token-level metrics and per-route usage. For marketplace we can provide a usage CSV or integrate with the marketplace metering API. We'll need the CloudMart metering spec.
[03:45] Liam (CloudMart): we send a metering API spec in the partner portal, we'll attach it to the PR.
[03:50] Diego: one implementation detail — when listing an image for private deploy, we include a startup script to configure network and KMS reference. We need a short template from CloudMart for metadata fields.
[04:05] Maya: will share the template.
[04:08] Alex: ok next, performance validation: Priya, can you talk about the staged perf run?
[04:14] Priya: sure, plan is to run a 2-hour smoke test on CloudMart staging: 100 concurrent users, typical prompt distribution, measure p99 latency and token cost. We'll prepare a small benchmark harness and share results in spreadsheet. Also will test cold start for model variants and quantized vs full precision.
[04:35] Ethan: do you have recommended hardware for the staging? We have a couple of GPU types — A10G and H100 — curious what Redwood needs for the model variants.
[04:45] Priya: H100 is ideal for throughput, A10G is fine for latency-sensitive small models. We'll include kernel selection recommendations in the RA — e.g., quantized 4-bit for A10G, optimizations for H100.
[04:58] Maya: note product wants the listing copy and screenshots by end of next week.
[05:03] Alex: noted. We can provide sample screenshots of console onboarding and per-route dashboards.
[05:10] Sofia: on compliance, we need clarity on data retention: can logs and inputs be deleted per customer request, and what's retention by default?
[05:20] Alex: default retention 90 days for logs, configurable longer for enterprise; for hosted we have a retention API and deletion requests can be handled; for private it's customer-managed. We'll skin this out in the security pack.
[05:34] Maya: great. A few edge-cases from product: what about fallback models if a customer exceeds dedicated capacity? Does Redwood provide fallback variants?
[05:43] Priya: yes, we support routing policies — auto-fallback to compatible cheaper variants or to hosted short-term while dedicated scales. We'll document policy examples in RA.
[05:58] Ethan: about entitlements, can marketplace control model versions per customer? We want to be able to sell different SKUs (low-latency vs economy).
[06:08] Alex: yes, the marketplace mapping can map SKU -> Redwood route/model version; that's how customers can choose different tiers.
[06:18] Maya: ok good. Let's capture action items: Alex to send RA + marketplace checklist, Priya to run perf tests, Sofia to send security Qs.
[06:28] Alex: adding Diego to the perf run for packaging and startup scripts.
[06:32] Diego: will prep the container/AMI template.
[06:36] Maya: timeline from partners is target listing in March; we'll confirm once we get the assets.
[06:42] Alex: sounds reasonable. Any blockers from CloudMart side?
[06:45] Liam: just need the manifest template and an estimated testing window.
[06:50] Alex: we'll propose dates in a follow-up.
[06:53] Priya: quick note, sometimes transcription says Kv cache or K V cache, we may use different names in docs — will standardize.
[07:02] Maya: good call, our marketplace docs prefer consistent naming.
[07:08] Alex: ok last items, we'll share a sample listing draft and security pack by EOD Friday next week, and schedule the perf run for week of 2/23.
[07:20] Sofia: thanks, we'll compile security Qs by Monday.
[07:25] Alex: any final questions?
[07:28] Ethan: none here.
[07:30] Maya: none. thanks all.
[07:33] Alex: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[07:36] END: approx 00:45:00 total

Notes on transcript quality: light transcription errors present (e.g., 'marketplace-hosed' vs 'marketplace-hosted', 'KV cache' miswritten as 'K V cache').
